issues.legal_issue: A registering authority cannot serve as a statutory attesting witness to prove a will when the attesting witnesses do not support its execution.
material_facts: The dispute concerned whether a will disposing of property was validly proved.
Neither of the two attesting witnesses supported the will’s execution.
The trial court relied on the registering authority’s statement to find that the will had been proved.
The lower appellate court and the High Court found that the Registrar could not be a statutory attesting witness.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the will had not been duly proved was correct, and the appeal concerning the agricultural property was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A Registrar cannot be treated as a statutory attesting witness to establish due execution of a will. The Court relied on M. L. Abdul Jabhar Sahib v. H. V. Venkata Sastri & Sons and Beni Chand (since dead) now by Lrs. v. Smt. Kamla Kunwar; the judgment does not identify specific statutory provisions.

predicates.will_validity_dispute: The proceeding disputes whether a will was validly proved.
predicates.attesting_witnesses_do_not_support_execu: The witnesses who attested the will do not support its execution.
predicates.proof_depends_on_registering_authority_a: A party relies on the registering authority as an attesting witness to prove the will.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns proof of a will, its attesting witnesses do not support execution, and proof depends on the registering authority as an attesting witness, the will is not duly proved.

issues.legal_issue: A claim to a share in a residential house may be dismissed when the claimant agrees to that disposition through counsel acting on instructions.
material_facts: During the hearing, the Court suggested that, in view of the plaintiff’s marriage, she should not claim a share in the residential house.
Counsel, acting on instructions, agreed that the decree could be modified and the suit concerning the house dismissed.
The Court granted special leave, allowed the appeal concerning the house, set aside the lower courts’ decree, and dismissed the suit as to her share in the house.
issues.conclusion: The decree was modified and the suit concerning the claimant’s share in the residential house was dismissed by agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court acted on counsel’s agreement, given on instructions, to modify the decree and dismiss the house claim. The judgment states no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this disposition.

predicates.residential_property_claim: The proceeding includes a claim to a share in a residential property.
predicates.claimant_agrees_through_counsel_to_dismi: Counsel, acting on the claimant’s instructions, agrees that the claim should be dismissed.

issues.definition: When a proceeding includes a claim to a share in a residential property and counsel acting on the claimant’s instructions agrees to dismissal, the claim is dismissed.
